title: Mathematical extraction of binding constants from electrophoretic selection data from DNA-Encoded Libraries
authors: Boris P Belotserkovskii; Patrick J Mcenaney; Victor A Galievsky; Kirill Novikov; Spurti U Akki; Divya Kanichar; Joshua L Turnbull; Virja A Pandya; Nikhil Jain; Jacob H Pachter; Vincent Lee; Ankita Biswas; Dong Min Mun; Nathaniel H Stanley; R Edward Watts
one_liner_zh: 该文从DNA编码文库电泳分离数据中提取结合常数，虽涉及蛋白-DNA互作但聚焦小分子-蛋白结合，非TF-DNA体系且无AI/物理模拟方法，仅理论建模，与课题关联有限。
abstract: DNA-encoded libraries (DELs) comprise up to billions of small molecules, enabling the discovery of binders to target proteins. Various selection techniques are used to isolate target binders and assess their binding properties. In our study, we focus on electrophoretic separation of DEL members in media uniformly filled with the target protein. Differences in the electrophoretic velocities of bound and unbound DEL members impact their spatial distribution in the medium. This distribution depends on the binding rate constant (kon) and the equilibrium dissociation constant (KD). We derive theoretical models to determine these constants from data acquired with our novel nDexer technique, and with capillary electrophoresis (CE), by analyzing the mean and variance of DEL members' spatial positions in nDexer, and their arrival times at a detector in capillary electrophoresis. Our findings align well with computer simulations and experimental results.
abstract_zh: DNA编码文库（DELs）包含多达数十亿的小分子，能够发现靶蛋白的结合物。多种筛选技术被用于分离靶标结合物并评估其结合特性。在我们的研究中，我们聚焦于在均匀填充靶蛋白的介质中对DEL成员进行电泳分离。结合与未结合的DEL成员在电泳速度上的差异影响它们在介质中的空间分布。这种分布取决于结合速率常数（kon）和平衡解离常数（KD）。我们推导了理论模型，以从我们新颖的nDexer技术和毛细管电泳（CE）获取的数据中确定这些常数，通过分析nDexer中DEL成员空间位置的均值和方差，以及它们在毛细管电泳中到达检测器的时间。我们的发现与计算机模拟和实验结果高度吻合。
